### Observed differences

- The dominant difference is an exchange of two groups of activities around the middle of the case. In the earlier window, a case ran A40, then exactly one of the three alternatives A19, A21 or A24 (each in roughly 30–36 of 100 cases; the three never ran together), then A25 and A29, then the trio A20, A22 and A23 — present in every case but in no fixed order — and finally A30. In the later window this is reversed: A40's outgoing transitions go to the trio A20/A22/A23 in about 83 of 100 cases (previously about 92 in 100 went to the alternatives), the trio now leads to A25 (about 28–37 in 100 of each member's outgoing transitions, where it previously led to A30 in similar shares), and A29 now leads to the alternatives A24/A19/A21 (about 98 in 100 combined, previously to the trio). [DIR019, DIR020, DIR021, DIR022, DIR023, DIR024, DIR029, DIR040, OCC019, OCC021, OCC024, REL048, REL051, REL070]

- Every cross-pair between the two groups reversed its order: A19 ran before A20 in about 29 of 100 cases earlier and in essentially none later, while A20 runs before A19 in about 33 of 100 cases in the later window; A21 ran before A20 in about 34 of 100 cases earlier, and A20 runs before A21 in about 28 of 100 later; A24 ran before A25 in about 35 of 100 earlier, and A25 runs before A24 in about 38 of 100 later. The same reversal holds for all other pairings of the two groups. [REL047, REL049, REL050, REL052, REL053, REL058, REL061, REL062, REL063, REL068, REL069, REL071, REL072, REL078, REL085, REL092, REL093]

- Event positions and step gaps mirror the swap: the mean position of A19, A21 and A24 moved from about 0.36–0.37 to about 0.67 of the case, while A20, A22 and A23 moved from about 0.64–0.65 to about 0.38–0.39. The A29-to-A30 gap shrank from about 4 steps to about 2, the A40-to-A25 gap grew from about 2 steps to about 4, the formerly common direct successions A40 → A21 and A21 → A25 practically disappeared, and A29 now runs directly into A21/A19, which in turn run directly into A30. [POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010, LAG035, LAG040, LAG041, LAG060, LAG061, LAG067, LAG069]

- The surrounding anchors kept their order — A40 still runs before both groups, A30 still after them, A25 still precedes A29 — and the internal character of both groups is unchanged: A20, A22 and A23 still appear in every case and in both orders in similar shares, and A19, A21 and A24 still never occur together, each keeping a share of roughly 30–39 of 100 cases. [OCC019, OCC020, OCC021, OCC022, OCC023, OCC024, REL054, REL055, REL059, REL060, REL077, REL098, REL103]

- A08 occurs in far fewer cases: about 64 in 100 earlier versus about 29 in 100 later (mean occurrences per trace about 0.68 versus 0.32). The detour A15 → A08 → A16 largely disappeared: A15's outgoing transitions to A08 fell from about 39 to about 7 in 100 while A15 → A16 rose from about 61 to about 88 in 100, and A08 → A16 fell from about 93 to about 31 in 100. Where A08 still runs, it sits later and much more variably in the case (mean event position about 0.26 versus 0.41; upper quartile about 0.26 versus 0.56). [OCC008, DIR008, DIR015, LAG004, POS001, REL001]

- Smaller shifts: in the late branch region, A42 now occurs in about 67 of 100 cases (up from about 62) while A43 and A44 occur slightly less often and repeat less (A43's repeat share fell from about 0.19 to 0.12), and A39 rose from about 49 to 57 of 100 cases; the rare activities A02, A04, A06 and A10 roughly doubled or tripled from low bases (about 7–9 to about 16–24 of 100 cases), though the later values rest on only about 32–47 traces each. [OCC002, OCC004, OCC006, OCC010, OCC036, OCC038, OCC039, OCC040, DIR041]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that two blocks of the process exchanged their position: the alternative step — exactly one of A19, A21, A24 per case — moved from between A40 and A25 to between A29 and A30, while the mandatory, unordered trio A20, A22, A23 moved from between A29 and A30 to between A40 and A25, with the surrounding wiring rewired accordingly (the alternatives now lead to A30 instead of A25, A29 feeds the alternatives instead of the trio, A40 feeds the trio instead of the alternatives, and the trio leads to A25 instead of A30). This is shown directly by the successor profiles of A19, A21, A24, A29 and A40, each backed by roughly 60–200 observations per window, and consistently by the order reversals in all cross-pairs, the opposite position shifts, and the gap changes; the new order was practically unobserved in the earlier window and the old order is practically unobserved in the later one, so this is a relocation of the blocks rather than a frequency shift between two coexisting orders. [DIR019, DIR020, DIR021, DIR022, DIR023, DIR024, DIR029, DIR040, REL047, REL058, REL062, REL063, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009, POS010, LAG035, LAG060, LAG061, LAG069]

Limitations: the many agreeing relation items describe one underlying reorder rather than independent confirmations, and with two samples of 200 cases the evidence cannot rule out that the windows mix case types that differ in block order (a case-mix difference) rather than a change in the routing itself; a few lag-based items rest on very few observations and were not relied on. [REL047, LAG026, LAG036]

Other differences: A08 occurs in far fewer cases (about 64 in 100 earlier, about 29 in 100 later) and the detour A15 → A08 → A16 has largely been replaced by a direct A15 → A16 transition, with A08 sitting later and more variably where it still runs; in the late branch region shares moved mildly towards A42 and away from A43 and A44, and A39 became somewhat more frequent; the rare activities A02, A04, A06 and A10 rose from small bases. [OCC008, DIR008, DIR015, POS001, OCC036, OCC038, OCC039, OCC040, DIR041, OCC002, OCC004, OCC006, OCC010]
